questions.question: Who is the founder of modern micro finance ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Yunus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Yunus** is recognized as the founder of modern microfinance.
 
• He established the **Grameen Bank** in Bangladesh in 1983, which provides small loans to the impoverished without requiring collateral.
 
• The concept of microfinance aims to empower the poor, especially women, by providing them with the means to start small businesses and improve their living conditions.
 
• Yunus’s innovative banking model has been replicated worldwide and has helped millions of people escape poverty.
 
• In recognition of his efforts, Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank were awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize** in 2006.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microfinance** refers to financial services, including loans, savings, insurance, and fund transfers, provided to low-income individuals or groups who typically lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• The **Grameen Bank** model is based on mutual trust, accountability, participation, and creativity.
 
• The success of microfinance institutions like the Grameen Bank has demonstrated that providing financial services to the poor can be a sustainable and profitable venture.
 
• Microfinance has been a powerful tool for social and economic development, contributing to poverty reduction, women's empowerment, and improved health and education outcomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

**C. Rangarajan**:

 
• C. Rangarajan is a distinguished Indian economist and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• He played a significant role in India's economic liberalization during the 1990s.
 
• Rangarajan has also served as the Chairman of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council.
 
• He is known for his contributions to macroeconomic policy and banking reforms in India.

**V.K.V. Rao**:

 
• V.K.V. Rao is a noted Indian economist with expertise in economic policy and planning.
 
• He has made significant contributions to the study of poverty, inequality, and regional disparities in India.
 
• Rao has held various academic and research positions, influencing public policy through his work.
 
• His research has been instrumental in shaping discussions around economic development and social welfare.

**Y.V. Reddy**:

 
• Y.V. Reddy is a prominent Indian economist and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• He is credited with steering India’s economy through the global financial crisis of 2008 with his prudent monetary policies.
 
• Reddy has also authored several books on banking, finance, and public policy.
 
• He is widely respected for his independent thinking and contributions to financial stability in India.

questions.question: Who among the following was primarily an integral part of the Indian National Army (INA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhas Chandra Bose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who led the Indian National Army (INA) against British colonial rule during World War II.
 
• The INA was initially formed in 1942 under Mohan Singh, but it gained significant momentum and recognition under the leadership of Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• Bose's leadership was instrumental in revitalizing the INA and garnering support from Indian expatriates in Southeast Asia.
 
• The INA played a crucial role in India's struggle for independence, inspiring many through its motto "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom."
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose's efforts and the INA's activities were pivotal in raising awareness and support for India's independence movement on an international scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was born on January 23, 1897, in Cuttack, Odisha, and was a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was known for his radical approach and differences with Mahatma Gandhi's more pacifist methods.
 
• In 1943, Bose proclaimed the establishment of the Provisional Government of Free India in Singapore, which was supported by the Axis powers during World War II.
 
• The INA's campaigns, particularly in the northeastern regions of India, are remembered for their bravery and the sacrifices made by its soldiers.
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose's legacy continues to inspire generations, and he is affectionately remembered as "Netaji" (Respected Leader) by millions of Indians.

questions.question: Which kind of computer security requires verifying the genuineness of the individuals or organisations that want to access a system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Authentication**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Authentication** is the process of verifying the identity of individuals or organizations attempting to access a system.
 
• It ensures that only genuine users can gain access to the system, thereby protecting it from unauthorized access.
 
• Common methods of authentication include passwords, biometric verification, and multi-factor authentication.
 
• Authentication is a critical component of computer security, alongside other aspects such as confidentiality, availability, and non-repudiation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Confidentiality** refers to protecting information from being accessed by unauthorized parties.
 
• **Availability** ensures that information and resources are accessible to authorized users when needed.
 
• **Non-repudiation** prevents individuals or entities from denying their actions or commitments in a digital context.
 
• Effective computer security requires a combination of these elements to ensure the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of information.

questions.question: As per Olympic rules, in the third game, badminton players change ends when a side scores _____ points.

• As per **Olympic rules**, badminton players change ends in the third game when a side scores **11 points**.

• Players also change ends at the end of the first game and at the end of the second game if a third game is to be played.

• According to the **BWF regulations**, the change of ends helps to maintain the balance and fairness of the game.
 
• The current scoring system in badminton is the 21-point rally scoring system, where players score a point on every serve, regardless of which side is serving.
 
• The BWF regularly updates the rules and regulations to enhance the sport and ensure fair play.

questions.question: A _________________ is a cloud of dust and gas inside a galaxy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nebula**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **nebula** is a cloud of dust and gas inside a galaxy.
 
• Nebulae are often regions where new stars are being formed.
 
• They can be composed of hydrogen, helium, and other ionized gases.
 
• Some of the well-known nebulae include the Eagle Nebula, the Orion Nebula, and the Crab Nebula.
 
• Nebulae can be observed in various colors depending on the elements they contain and the types of radiation they emit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term "nebula" was originally used to describe any diffuse astronomical object, including galaxies beyond the Milky Way.
 
• Modern astronomy distinguishes between different types of nebulae, such as emission nebulae, reflection nebulae, and dark nebulae.
 
• Emission nebulae glow brightly due to the ionization of their gases by nearby high-energy stars.
 
• Reflection nebulae do not emit their own light but reflect the light of nearby stars.
 
• Dark nebulae are dense clouds of gas and dust that block the light from objects behind them.

questions.question: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Five types of writs** can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens.
 
• These writs are: **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto,** and **Certiorari**.
 
• The power to issue these writs is granted to the Supreme Court under **Article 32** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is issued to produce a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court and to set them free if such detention is found illegal.
 
• The writ of **Mandamus** commands a public authority to perform a public duty.
 
• The writ of **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• The writ of **Quo-Warranto** is issued to prevent a person from holding a public office to which they are not entitled.
 
• The writ of **Certiorari** is issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court for review.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution is known as the "Heart and Soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• It provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of violation of Fundamental Rights.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power to issue writs not only for Fundamental Rights but also for other purposes under **Article 139** of the Constitution.
 
• Similarly, the High Courts have the power to issue writs under **Article 226** of the Constitution.
 
• The writ jurisdiction of the High Courts is broader as it is not confined to the protection of Fundamental Rights alone.

questions.question: _________ is a significant festival of the Parsi people who practice Zoroastrianism as it marks the birth anniversary of Zoroaster.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khordad Sal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khordad Sal** is a significant festival celebrated by the Parsi community, who practice Zoroastrianism.
 
• This festival marks the birth anniversary of **Zoroaster**, the founder of Zoroastrianism.
 
• It is a day of thanksgiving and celebration, where Parsis engage in prayers, feasting, and community activities.
 
• The festival is observed with great fervor and is considered one of the most important events in the Zoroastrian calendar.
 
• On this day, Zoroastrians reflect on the teachings of Zoroaster and reaffirm their commitment to the principles of good thoughts, good words, and good deeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoroastrianism** is one of the world's oldest monotheistic religions, dating back to the 6th century BCE in ancient Persia.
 
• The religion emphasizes the duality of good and evil and the importance of individual choice in promoting good.
 
• Zoroaster, also known as Zarathustra, is considered a prophet and a spiritual leader who reformed the ancient religious practices of Persia.
 
• The Parsi community in India is one of the largest groups of Zoroastrians globally, having migrated from Persia to avoid religious persecution.
 
• Other important festivals for Zoroastrians include **Jamshed-e-Navroz** (the Persian New Year) and **Pateti** (the last day of the Zoroastrian year).

questions.question: The loss of water in the form of water droplets from leaves of plants is called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guttation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guttation** is the process by which water is expelled from the edges of leaves of certain plants in the form of droplets.
 
• This occurs primarily during the night when soil moisture levels are high, and transpiration is low.
 
• It is different from **transpiration**, which is the evaporation of water from plant surfaces, mainly through stomata.
 
• Guttation usually occurs through specialized structures called **hydathodes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pressure gradient** refers to the difference in hydrostatic pressure that drives the movement of water and nutrients within plant tissues.
 
• **Plasmolysis** is the process where cells lose water in a hypertonic solution, causing the cell membrane to pull away from the cell wall.
 
• **Translocation** is the movement of nutrients and other solutes within the plant, typically through the phloem.
 
• The process of guttation is most commonly observed in **grasses, strawberries, and some herbaceous plants**.

questions.question: In MS Word, which feature allows you to create different headers and footers for odd and even pages in a document?

• **Different Odd & Even Pages** is a feature in MS Word that allows you to create distinct headers and footers for odd and even pages in a document.

• Understanding and utilizing these features can enhance the professionalism and readability of your documents.

questions.question: By which ministry of Government of India was the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana** was started by the **Ministry of Rural Development** of the Government of India.
 
• This scheme aims to uplift the urban and rural poor by enhancing sustainable livelihood opportunities through skill development.
 
• It encompasses both the **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)** and the **National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM)**.
 
• The scheme is named after **Deendayal Upadhyaya**, an Indian philosopher, economist, and politician, who was one of the key leaders of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, the forerunner of the present-day Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• The primary goal of the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana is to reduce poverty by enabling the poor households to access gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities, resulting in an appreciable improvement in their livelihoods on a sustainable basis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ministry of Rural Development** is responsible for the implementation and oversight of rural development programs in India.
 
• It works towards improving the quality of life and economic well-being of people living in rural areas.
 
• Key initiatives under the Ministry include the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin)**, **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, and **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**.
 
• The Ministry also focuses on promoting social inclusion, gender equity, and sustainable development.
 
• It collaborates with various state governments, non-governmental organizations, and international agencies to achieve its objectives.
